contentBlocks.text: This week you've explored traits offspring get from their parents. Today: not everything is inherited — some things are learned instead!

An inherited trait is something an offspring is born with, passed from its parents — like fur color or eye color. A learned behavior is something an animal or person learns to do after being born — like a dog learning to sit, or a person learning to ride a bike. A puppy is born with its fur color (inherited), but it learns tricks over time (learned). Sort these into inherited or learned: a bird's feather color, a dog knowing how to fetch, a person's eye color, a person knowing how to read.
You now understand the real difference between something you're born with and something you learn! Tomorrow we'll review everything from this week.

objectives: Distinguish an inherited trait from a learned behavior
Correctly sort four examples into inherited or learned
teacherGuide.facilitationScript:
1. Review this week's resemblance and variation content.
2. Introduce inherited traits vs. learned behaviors using the puppy fur-color/tricks example.
3. Sort the four examples together.
4. Complete the worksheet.
5. Close by having the child name one more inherited trait and one more learned behavior of their own.
differentiationTips: Struggling: focus on just two clearly contrasting examples (fur color vs. a trained trick) before adding the other two
Ready for more: ask the child to explain why reading is learned even though humans are naturally capable of learning language
This inherited-vs-learned distinction is a genuinely important early-science concept, worth real discussion time
teacherGuide.answerKey: Inherited: a bird's feather color, a person's eye color. Learned: a dog knowing how to fetch, a person knowing how to read.
teacherGuide.standardsRationale: Directly addresses NGSS Grade 1 standard 1-LS3-1's explicit note that some characteristics are learned behaviors rather than inherited traits — a real, important scientific distinction.
